# Offline receive audit — implementation notes

## Layout

* `offline.Main` — unchanged starter adapter: decodes the internal ASCII metadata emitted by the
  public `format_io` validator and prints exactly one JSON value.
* `offline.ReceiveAudit` — the whole pipeline: datagram/envelope framing, packet-number
  reconstruction, routing/key/range/authentication/duplication/key-epoch precedence, the frame
  decoder, one packet transaction per envelope, canonical envelope re-encoding, hashing and the
  snapshot report. Supporting structures live in it: `Store` (sparse byte ledger per stream/crypto
  level), `Ledger` (merged half-open intervals for acknowledged ranges and retired local sequences),
  `Cur` (varint/byte cursor with the shortest-encoding rule for frame types) and the journal of
  undo closures that makes a packet atomic.
* `de.rub.nds.*` — retained TLS-Attacker codec, repaired (see below);
  `VariableLengthIntegerEncoding` is the canonical varint encoder used by `ReceiveAudit`.

## Codec repairs

* Frame DTOs no longer narrow QUIC varints to `int`: `ModifiableInteger` counters/ids/offsets became
  `ModifiableLong` with `long` setters, so values up to 2^62-1 survive parse and re-serialize.
* `AckFrame` keeps every subsequent (gap, range) pair; `AckFrameParser` stores them and
  `AckFrameSerializer` writes them instead of dropping all but the first range.
* `StreamFrameParser` no longer invents an offset when the OFF flag is clear, and
  `StreamFrameSerializer` now selects the offset/length fields from the STREAM flag bits instead of
  nullable DTO fields; lengthless frames stay lengthless.
* Length-driven reads use `Parser.parseLongByteArrayField`, so a declared length larger than the
  remaining bytes is an end-of-stream error rather than a narrowed int.
* `ConnectionCloseFrameSerializer` always emits the reason length field.
* `PaddingFrameParser` consumes one zero byte per frame (the frame layer owns the type byte), which
  matches "each padding byte remains one zero".
* Round-trip coverage for every retained frame type lives in the development harness
  (`tmp/dev/codec/CodecTest.java`, not part of the artifact).

## Contract decisions that the prose leaves open

* `packet` in `packets`/`closed` rows is the header attempt index inside its own datagram event
  (`event` is the trace-wide event index, so key events still consume an index).
* Initial/Handshake packets authenticate only from an annotation whose value is `0`; any other
  non-null value or a null annotation is `AUTH`.
* `closed.code` is the same status token used in `packets` (`PEER_CLOSE`, `KEY_UPDATE_ERROR`,
  `FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR`, ...).
* A datagram row always reports `sha256`; when nothing was accepted it is the standard empty digest.
* Send references to client bidi ids perform the same limit check and implicit opening as receive
  references, while send references to client unidirectional ids are `STREAM_STATE_ERROR`.

## Development cross-check

`tmp/dev/ref.py` is an independent Python model of PROTOCOL.md used only to diff against the
compiled pipeline on structured and randomized traces (`tmp/dev/fuzz2.py`, `tmp/dev/fuzz3.py`);
`python3 /workspace/check.py /workspace/submission/src` passes on the public fixtures.
EOF
